Full pool mean combination to compare against trimmed_mean.
Median of top transform-based models to leverage stability and reduce outlier impact.

The current leader (trimmed_mean) suggests robustness is key due to ranking instability. However, the median on a curated pool performed well, implying that reducing variance via pooling is effective. I will test a weighted combination using inverse_error weights on the top-performing models identified in the error table (top 6), which are less correlated than the full pool and explicitly selected for their low RMSE. This tests if error-based weighting can outperform simple robust aggregation on a high-quality subset.

The current leader (a1) uses a trimmed mean on the full pool to handle the unstable ranking and strong trend. The runner-up (a4) uses inverse-error weighting on a smaller, high-performing subset (pool5). Since the series is trend-dominated but has no outliers and unstable rankings, I will test a robust combination that leverages the diversity of the top-ranked models from different correlation groups (CWT and DWT domains) using a weighted approach that adapts to their recent performance (error_trend), which may better capture the non-stationary dynamics than static inverse_error.
Testing simple mean over top 6 models to check robustness against unstable ranking and reduce variance from weighted methods.

The current leader (mean on pool6) performs well but the ranking stability is low (tau=0.29), suggesting simple averaging might be fragile if the "best" model shifts. I will test a weighted combination using `inverse_error` weights, which down-weights poorer models and may offer better robustness than equal weighting given the unstable ranking. I'll use the top 6 models from pool6 which have shown strong individual performance.

The current leader (mean on pool6) performs well but is statistically indistinguishable from a weighted variant. To break this tie and explore robustness, I will test DBA (Dynamic Time Warping Barycenter Averaging) on the full pool, which explicitly minimizes variance across all models including those with lower individual scores but potentially complementary error structures. This addresses the 'unstable ranking' characteristic by leveraging geometric averaging rather than simple arithmetic or inverse-error weighting.

The current leader (mean on pool6) is strong but the ranking stability is low (tau=0.29), suggesting that simple averaging might dilute the best models or include redundant ones. I will test a robust median combination over the top 6 models from the previous best-performing pool to see if it mitigates the instability better than the mean, leveraging the "robust" hint in the decision card for this trend-dominated series.

The series has high trend strength and unstable ranking (tau=0.29). The leader 'mean on pool6' performs well, but given the instability, a robust combination like DBA or a wider mean over complementary transforms might help. I will try DBA on the top-performing transform models (pool4) to see if it reduces variance compared to simple mean.

The series has high trend strength and unstable ranking (tau=0.29). The leader 'a6' uses a simple mean on a curated pool of 6 models. To improve robustness against the unstable ranking while potentially capturing more signal, I will test an inverse-error weighted combination on the full pool of 19 models. This leverages the highest-performing models (like DWT_catboost) with greater weight while keeping the diversity of the full pool to mitigate the risk of any single model failing in the blind test.

The series has high trend strength and unstable ranking (tau=0.29). The leader 'a6' uses a simple mean on pool6. I want to test if a robust combination like DBA (Density Based Averaging) on the top models provides better stability against the noise in the validation windows, specifically checking if it handles the recent shift in best model performance better than the mean.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.3716. Series context: trend strength 0.8039 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.29); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 28.401.
